resources.string: Tap Connect. On a Zontes 368G, open MotoPlay on the dash and leave that screen up.
Starting Android Auto on the phone. Stay next to the bike.
Joining the bike Wi-Fi. Stay close and leave MotoPlay open.
Wi-Fi is up. Looking for the dashboard…
Dashboard found. Linking Android Auto — this takes a few seconds.
Streaming to the dash. You can pocket the phone.
Mirroring the phone screen onto the dash.
The link dropped. Leave MotoPlay open — trying again.
The bike is out of range. Turn the ignition on and stay nearby.
Stopped. Tap Connect when you are ready to ride.
Couldn\'t finish linking. Turn the ignition off, wait 5 seconds, turn it on, open MotoPlay, then tap Connect.
The phone is not on the bike Wi-Fi. Turn Wi-Fi on, wake the dash, and tap Connect again.
Bike Wi-Fi joined, but the dashboard did not answer. Open MotoPlay, or turn the ignition off and on, then retry.
Android Auto did not start. In the Android Auto app, open the menu and start the head unit server, then tap Connect.
A VPN is blocking the bike network. Turn the VPN off for this ride, then tap Connect.
This dash joins your phone hotspot. Turn the hotspot on with the name and password shown on the dash, then retry.
A permission is still missing. Allow Nearby devices, turn Bluetooth on, then tap Connect again.
Something blocked the link. Restart the ignition, keep MotoPlay open, and tap Connect. If it keeps failing, open Help and share the logs.
On a Samsung phone (such as the Galaxy S23 Ultra), also turn off battery limits for this app and leave Wi-Fi on.

The official CFMoto or EasyConnect app is holding the bike\'s link, so the dash stays blank. Close it, then connect again.\n\nClose & retry tries to stop it. If the dash is still blank, open App settings and tap Force stop.
Something else is holding the bike\'s link. Close any other CFMoto or EasyConnect app, then tap Connect.

Android Auto reached the phone, but a VPN is blocking the bike Wi-Fi.

Try one of these, then tap Connect again:
• Turn the VPN off for this ride
• Turn off Always-on VPN and "Block connections without VPN"
• Allow the local network in the VPN app
The app closed unexpectedly last time. The log was saved — open Logs and tap Share logs so the problem can be seen.

Entire screen works best while riding. Screen fit and mirror orientation are in Setup.

A single app must stay in front; Android sends no frames when it is in the background.

Bike touch does not control mirrored apps. Continue connects and sends this app to the background.
Hold detection off — a long press counts as a tap
Shared logs will include secrets — turn this off before posting them
Replace bike tuning for %1$s — profile, resolution, fit, power, margins, handlebar buttons, and Wi-Fi transport?\n\nPersonal preferences are left alone. Wi-Fi passwords are never imported.
